title: Native gluing builds surfaces, and four knots see only the surface
claim: Hub-free networks of three-place relations (every shared variable in exactly two copies) are pants decompositions of compact orientable surfaces with Euler characteristic minus the number of copies; two-place relations give only paths and cycles. A symmetric three-place relation glues topologically, as a relation or with witness counts, exactly when two glued copies give a result symmetric in its four legs. Among the 34 knots exactly four glue topologically with counts: the two parity knots (leg total fixed, 2^genus witnesses, one hidden bit per handle) and the two 'no lone value' knots (sphere: no single leg carries the lone value; any handle frees everything; closed genus-g counts tr H^(g-1), H = [[3,1],[1,2]], eigenvalue ratio the golden ratio squared); the two frozen knots forget once glued; not-all-equal and the 27 asymmetric knots see more than the surface. All-equal, the hub, glues topologically but is not a knot.
failure_conditions: A hub-free network whose glued result or witness counts differ from the profile of its genus and boundary for a relation classified as topological.
A relation classified as not topological whose four-leg composite is symmetric, or the converse.
foundation_claim_scope: Finite Boolean relations glued along shared variables; surfaces are read from the gluing pattern, not drawn. No physical space is claimed.

validation.status: checked: prose proof (elementary: Euler characteristic, generalized associativity, linear algebra over GF(2), an induction for the no-lone relations); check.py (standard library) enumerates all connected hub-free networks with up to six copies (220 shapes up to isomorphism) and confirms the census of all 16 symmetric relations, the four-leg criterion, the parity and no-lone formulas, the frozen certificate, the knot census and three controls. No human or external review
validation.level: V1 prose proof with exhaustive checks up to six copies
